registration: node: pixel (i, j) is at x = xMin + i*cellSize, z = zMin + j*cellSize; row 0 = north (zMin)
encoding: rg16: elevation_m = (R*256 + G) * scale + offset; B = trust mask (0..255)

localDatumNote: River sites model heights above a single 'modelled high water' (y = 0). localDatumOffset 2.0 m OD is a compromise high-water level across the timeline: Roman high water at the City is published as no more than about +1.5 m OD (Taylor, London Archaeologist 16(1)), and present Mean High Water Springs is about +3.5 to +4.5 m OD.
notes: UPLAND RELIEF ONLY. The river corridor is utterly changed since 1625 (embankments, reclaimed foreshore, docks, made ground several metres thick, canalised Brent, railways), so this grid must not replace the river and bank model. It is the DTM with modern works masked and filled, then smoothed with a 25 m Gaussian, and B = trust (0 near the river and works, on ground below about 5-6.5 m OD, 1 on the terraces). Even on the trusted ground the modern surface includes made ground (several metres in the City), so treat absolute levels as an upper bound on the natural surface and use the shape (relative relief) first.
